collection.description: A family of termites has moved into the village, and nobody noticed until a door frame turned to powder in someone's hand.

ask.text:
A family of termites has moved into the village, and nobody noticed until a door frame turned to powder in someone's hand. Now (name), the best builder, has gone round knocking on every post with a stone, and too many of them sound hollow.
There are two ways to deal with termites, the old builders say. Smoke them out with a fire of bitter leaves, which works but smells so bad the village will have to sleep on the beach for three nights. Or replace every hollow post with ironwood, which termites can't eat, but which means a lot of work for everyone.
Which should (name) choose?

c1o1.text: Three nights on the beach, listening to the waves and complaining about the smell. On the fourth morning, the termites are gone, and the builders patch every chewed post with fresh wood. The huts smell of bitter leaves for a month. Nobody minds, because they don't fall down.

c1o2.text: While the smoke does its work, the builders sit on the beach and argue about posts, and joints, and how to keep termites out for good. When they go back up, they don't just patch, they rebuild: raised stones under every post, gaps the termites can't cross. Every builder in the village comes out of it better at the job.

c1.text: The whole village carries its sleeping mats down to the beach, and (name) lights the bitter-leaf fires. The smoke is yellow, and smells like burnt hair and rotten fruit...

c2o1.text: It takes two weeks of aching backs and blistered hands, but at the end of it every hut in the village stands on ironwood. The termites move out in disgust, and go and live in a dead tree in the forest, where they belong. "Built to last," says (name), knocking on a post. It rings like a bell.

c2o2.text: Two weeks of carrying ironwood is too much for (name). By the end of it, every post is replaced and the village is safe, but (name) is so sick of posts, hauling, knocking and wood that (he/she) hands the job over to the next best builder and takes up fishing. "I've built enough," (he/she) says. "Let someone else knock on things."

c2.text: Everyone who can carry wood heads up into the hills where the ironwood grows. It is so heavy it takes four people to carry one post...
